title: NanoSIMS analysis finds anomalous magnesium isotope ratios in Ubatuba fragments

tellings.quote: And one of them was anomalous. The magnesium ratios were way off.
>> So, yeah, we did a we did a mass spectrometry analysis of some of those pieces with a highly sensitive instrument. And one of them was anomalous. The magnesium ratios were way off.
tellings.difference: Calls the instrument a highly sensitive mass spectrometer rather than naming NanoSIMS.
tellings.link_reason: The same isotope analysis of the Ubatuba pieces at Stanford by Nolan, which found anomalous magnesium ratios.

as_told.title: Mass-spectrometry analysis of the Ubatuba pieces

plain: One of the metal fragments from Ubatuba, in Brazil, which the 2021 episode's title calls "Parts Of an Alien UFO", had magnesium that was mixed in the wrong proportions, says the Stanford scientist Garry Nolan, who ran the tests himself. He tells Michels that his team used a very sensitive instrument at Stanford, which can weigh the different forms of an element in a tiny sample, and that "one of them was anomalous. The magnesium ratios were way off," which, if true, would point to metal not made in the ordinary way. Telling it again on a 2026 episode, he calls the instrument simply a highly sensitive mass spectrometer.
